title: How Regan Hillyer Built her Empire
overview: Joining from Bali at 1am, Regan Hillyer sat down with Vishen Lakhiani to trace her path from a 23-year-old attendee at a Mindvalley event to a business on track for around $50 million this year. Vishen drew the entire manifesting funnel on screen, from three-minute videos and quizzes through the masterclass, autoresponder emails and a $5,000 Mastery, and Regan explained how she mirrors the same architecture in her own business, right up to a $1 million coaching package. You also heard her honest answers on content days she skips, how she handles overwhelm, and what keeps her building.
key_ideas: Regan's growth: when she first came to a Mindvalley event more than ten years ago she was doing just over $100,000 a year. Today her company is on track for around $50 million this year, built layer by layer over 14 years.

Claim your crown. Regan and Vishen looked up 'manifesting' as an industry years ago, found there was nothing there, and decided to claim the space. Nobody appoints you the expert; you choose the crown you put on and then get guidance on how to wear it.

The mindset shift that scaled the business was connecting it to something bigger than herself. Around the first $1 to 3 million most founders realise they can have everything they want and ask 'why keep going?'; Regan's answer was to leave the planet better than she found it. Her end game is to impact over a billion people, and every decision becomes a simple question: does this move the dial closer to that vision, or is it a distraction?

Service comes before scale. In 2018, when a Mindvalley cacao ceremony ran out of space, Regan rented a yoga studio and bought cacao with her own money so 250 people could attend for free; that is when Vishen gave her a bigger stage, and within two years of publishing her first programme, The Art of Manifesting became the number one programme on Mindvalley. Vishen calls this expansion energy: some teachers make everything they touch grow, while others meet every idea with 'but what if?'. Regan sets a deliberate intention to be a category of one, and her ratings are not luck.

Vishen's manifesting funnel, which does around $20 million a year: three-minute videos, Google search ads and a quiz lead to a page showing the free, mid-tier and high-end stack. Most people take the free masterclass; 1 to 3% buy the course or subscription, and the other 97% enter a 14-day autoresponder that gives away the best lessons and the best meditation. Then 21 days after purchase students are offered Lifebook, over three months they see $2,000 weekend classes, and around six months in they are invited to a summit where Manifesting Mastery ($5,000) is offered, typically a $5 million launch with a satisfaction score above 80. Timing, not pushing.

Collect stories. The Art of Manifesting has 172 published student stories and Manifesting Mastery 286. Vishen values each story at $5,000 to $10,000 because customers bring in more customers. Regan says not capturing client wins five to seven years ago cost her a lot of money.

Regan's two fundamentals: get your clients crazy results (over-deliver massively on free and low-ticket offers at $22, $55 and $97 so trust builds fast) and have a very clear sales pathway. Her offers step from free to a $100,000 mastermind, a $200,000 platinum container and a $1 million one-on-one coaching package, built layer by layer over 14 years; one container she started four and a half months ago has seen its clients generate over $64 million in cash between them.

On hard days Regan simply does not create content and renegotiates the deadline with her team. On overwhelm: write every item out, find the one thing that creates movement, and remind yourself the world will not explode if the list waits until tomorrow.

frameworks.name: The manifesting funnel (as drawn by Vishen)
steps: Traffic: three-minute videos, Google search ads and a quiz such as 'What is your manifesting archetype?'
Audience page showing the product stack: free (masterclass, e-book), mid-tier (courses and subscription, summit), high-end (Mastery at $5,000)
Free masterclass, built on the formula taught earlier in the summit
1 to 3% buy the course or the subscription; the other 97% receive a free e-book
14-day autoresponder giving the best lessons and the best meditation from the course for free
21 days after purchase, introduce a second product (Lifebook, a goal-setting programme)
Over 3 months, introduce related $2,000 weekend classes
Around 6 months, invite to a summit where the $5,000 Mastery is offered
Collect and publish student stories throughout; each one brings new customers

frameworks.name: Regan's two fundamentals
steps: Get your clients really crazy results: over-deliver on free and low-ticket offers ($22, $55, $97) so they get a fast result and trust you
Have a very clear sales pathway from free to your highest offer, with a next step for anyone not yet ready ('not ready for $10,000? here is the $2,000 offer')

frameworks.name: Regan's story engine
steps: Capture every client win and story as it happens
Feed the stories to your marketing team
Turn them into social media posts
Give them to the sales team so they can answer objections with a real story
Let the system compound so it grows without you

frameworks.name: Regan's overwhelm reset
steps: Recognise overwhelm is just your system trying to process too many options at once
Write everything in your head out on paper or in a journal, until the list is complete (Regan's often hit 37 items)
Ask: what is the one thing right now that will create movement in my company? Usually an offer, a sales process or a client result
Commit to that one or two things only
Tell yourself: if the rest is not done today, the world will not explode. Breathe and do it tomorrow

frameworks.name: The product step ladder (Vishen's recap)
steps: Each offer is roughly 5X the previous: $99, then $500, then $5,000, then $25,000
The best teachers extend it further: Regan goes to $100,000, then $250,000, then $1 million
The higher rungs are justified by the value delivered, for example helping a CEO grow a $100 million company by 10%

quotes.speaker: Regan Hillyer
quotes.text: You have to choose what crown you are putting on, right? No one's going to put that on you.

quotes.speaker: Regan Hillyer
quotes.text: At the end of the day, there's only you, your vibration, your frequency, your gifts, your life story, your talents. No one else is gonna do it quite like you.

quotes.speaker: Regan Hillyer
quotes.text: I realized that overwhelm is just your system trying to process too many options all at once

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: There's a certain energy in a human being that causes everything they touch to expand.

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: And that's what I really love about this business, because you're not being pushy. Even people who don't buy from you, you are still changing their lives.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: You look amazing, as always. Regan, where in the world are you right now, and what's going on there?

dialogue.speaker: Regan Hillyer
dialogue.text: I'm in Bali, Indonesia. I just finished two events: I surprised one of my mastermind communities with a four-day retreat and basically threw them a party, then I flew 21 of my team members in and for three days I celebrated them. There was one rule: we don't talk about work, we celebrate the vision and everything we're creating.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Here's the crazy story about Regan: at one point she was completely broke. I was living in Malaysia, where I take my family to Sunday brunch and invite anyone along, and Regan joined us at 23; I told her to attend the Mindvalley event, she did, she kept coming, and one day I put her on stage. Look at these pictures: a standing ovation a few months ago, Jay Shetty handing her the award in Dubai in January 2025 for the most popular programme on Mindvalley, The Art of Manifesting, and then Regan 12 years ago, sitting in the audience with half her head shaved. Today, at 36, she owns 700 acres in Costa Rica and is building a wellness resort, so before the nitty-gritty, share with the audience what you've built and why this is such an interesting career path.

dialogue.speaker: Regan Hillyer
dialogue.text: When I first came on that stage I was such a baby, and I've really grown up with Mindvalley; I've built a massive company on my own back end, but when I ask people where they first heard of me, it's Mindvalley, Mindvalley, Mindvalley. At that first event I'd just started my company and was doing just over $100,000 a year, and now we're on track for around $50 million this year, in a ten-year period. But my company wouldn't have grown unless I had claimed the space of being the expert in manifesting: people call me the queen of manifesting, and I tell them you have to choose what crown you are putting on, because no one is going to put it on you. I remember sitting in your apartment years ago looking up manifesting as an industry, finding it wasn't really there, and deciding we needed to claim it.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Let me play a video from 2018, when Regan's cacao ceremony at a Mindvalley event drew so many people that we ran out of space; with her own money she rented a yoga studio and bought cacao, and 250 people crammed in for free. When I see a teacher who is there to serve, I know it's not just about the money, so I gave her a bigger stage the next year, she got a standing ovation, and that's when I asked, 'If we published a programme with you, what would we call it?' I also told her I suspected she had a certain energy: there's an energy in a human being that causes everything they touch to expand, and another that causes everything to shrink and hit barriers, and within two years her first programme became the number one programme on Mindvalley. Many experts meet every idea with 'but what if this?', while Regan is constantly looking at what could expand.

dialogue.speaker: Regan Hillyer
dialogue.text: I'm looking at what could expand, and it's very intentional. When your team noticed my talks are always so highly rated and asked whether I set an intention around that, I said, of course: I want to deliver the best content possible because I want to be of the most useful service, so why would I not set an intention for mastery? You can be just another teacher, or you can choose to claim your place and be a category of one, because there's only one of you, your frequency, your gifts, your life story. Any rating or how well a programme does is not luck or chance; all of the manifestation energy is zeroed in on it.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Now let me show the audience what the Regan Hillyer business looks like on Mindvalley. Traffic comes from three-minute videos of Regan, Google search ads and a quiz, all leading to a page that shows our manifesting stack of free, mid-tier and high-end; most people go to the free masterclass, only 1 to 3% buy the course or subscription, and the other 97% go into a 14-day autoresponder where we give away the best lessons and the best meditation from the course. Then 21 days after they buy we introduce Lifebook, over three months we introduce $2,000 weekend classes, and around six months in we invite them to a manifesting summit where they can join Manifesting Mastery at $5,000, typically a $5 million launch with a satisfaction score over 80, while collecting stories all the way (172 for The Art of Manifesting, 286 for the Mastery, each worth another $5,000 to $10,000 to us). That's how we do 20 million a year in manifesting, so Regan, how do you leverage this traffic and build your $50 million business on your end?

dialogue.speaker: Regan Hillyer
dialogue.text: It's very similar on my back end. We never front up with a mastermind or a multi-thousand-dollar programme; we come in at free or with low-ticket offers at $22, $55 or $97, and my hack is to massively over-deliver, because if I can get someone a fast result at $22 they build trust and the next step at $2,000, $5,000 or $50,000 becomes a no-brainer. If someone isn't ready for a $10,000 offer, no problem, there's a $2,000 offer over here; timing is everything. Two things make it work: get your clients really crazy results, and have a very clear sales pathway. And the testimonials: five to seven years ago I wasn't capturing client stories and it cost me so much money, so now they feed my marketing team, then social media, then the sales team, and the whole engine compounds without me.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Regan, what is your highest value offering?

dialogue.speaker: Regan Hillyer
dialogue.text: A million-dollar one-on-one premium coaching package. A layer down is my platinum mastermind container at $200,000 for the year, where clients get my phone number and we chat daily, then a mastermind around $100,000, and then all the way down to $55, $22 and free. That range wasn't built overnight; it's a 14-year build of layer after layer, listening to clients and scaling as they scale. One container I started four and a half months ago, created because clients kept asking for help with certain things, and between them those clients have since generated over $64 million in cash.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Pay attention to that: remember the product step ladder, where every offer goes up by 5X, $99, $500, $5,000, $25,000? Regan takes it further, to $100,000, a quarter million and one million, and if you're a CEO responsible for $100 million in revenue and Regan can tweak your mindset so your company grows by 10%, that's worth a million. Now some questions I think trip our audience up: do you ever have days where you just don't want to create content, and what do you do on those days?

dialogue.speaker: Regan Hillyer
dialogue.text: I just don't create content on those days. I'm a human. Sometimes my team says, 'We need these five videos by Monday,' and if I don't feel like it I say, 'I can get them to you by Wednesday,' and we adjust in the flow. If something is really important, like Mindvalley needing me at 1am, I break my rules and show up. Other times the videos can wait 24 hours until I'm in a better flow.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: How do you deal with overwhelm? Do you ever experience it?

dialogue.speaker: Regan Hillyer
dialogue.text: Not so much anymore, but I used to, especially early on when I was the whole team, the marketing department, the sales, the content creation. I realised overwhelm is just your system trying to process too many options at once. So I'd sit down and write out everything in my head until there were 37 things on the list, then ask, 'What is the one thing right now that will create movement in my company?' It usually came back to an offer, a sales process or helping a client get a great result. I'd commit to that one or two things and tell myself, 'Regan, if the 37-point list isn't done today, the world's not going to explode. Breathe, do it tomorrow.'

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: And the final question, Regan. What's the end game? What legacy are you looking to leave on the planet?

dialogue.speaker: Regan Hillyer
dialogue.text: To impact over a billion people, and for them to realise they can create their most ideal reality, that they don't have to trade one thing off for another, and that they can have it all on their terms. When you're aligned like that, life gets very simple. An opportunity shows up and the question is: does this move the dial closer to that vision, or is it a distraction? It's a simple yes or no, and sometimes 'that's big and scary, but I'm going to do it anyway.'

exercises.name: The overwhelm list
exercises.instructions: When you feel overloaded, write every task and idea in your head onto one page. Then circle the single item that would create the most movement in your business, usually an offer, a sales process or a client result, and commit to that alone today.

next_steps: Decide what crown you are putting on: write the one-line space you are claiming as the expert, then say it out loud to someone this week.
Map your own sales pathway from free to your highest offer, and make sure there is a 'not ready yet? go here' step at every rung.
Pick your best single lesson or meditation and give it away in your follow-up emails to the people who did not buy.
Set up a simple system to capture every client win as it happens and route it to your marketing and sales.
attribution_notes: This transcript was already labelled 'Vishen:', 'Regan Hillyer:' and 'Mindvalley:'. The labels were checked against content and held up throughout: the 'Mindvalley:' passages are Jason Goldberg hosting (introducing Regan, recalling meeting her at A-Fest 2016, running the chat, handing to Vishen), Vishen's lines contain his questions, the funnel walkthrough and Mindvalley figures, and Regan's lines are first-person about her team, offers, clients and prices. Vishen's opening two lines are the close of his previous session, which is why they precede Jason's introduction. The only unclear moment is a garbled sign-off from Regan at the very end, which was omitted. Regan's reference to a Mindvalley team member who asked about her ratings has been kept but the name removed.
